jsonLdParsed.description: Dr. Autoimmune provides expert functional medicine and telehealth services focusing on chronic and autoimmune conditions for patients in Boulder and nationwide.

review.reviewBody:
Working with Dr. Ian at Dr. Autoimmune has truly been life‑changing. From our very first interaction, he made me feel heard, validated, and understood—something I had been missing for years in my health journey.

Dr. Ian took the time to really listen to my struggles and ailments, connected the dots, and focused on finding the root cause instead of just treating symptoms. His approach gave me clarity, hope, and—most importantly—my quality of life back.

I spent years searching for the right practitioner, and I can confidently say that Dr. Ian was worth every bit of the investment. His knowledge, compassion, and dedication to healing the whole body are unmatched. I cannot recommend working with him enough to anyone who feels stuck, dismissed, or exhausted trying to find answers.

If you’re looking for someone who truly understands how to help the body heal, Dr. Ian is it.

I’ve been a patient of Dr Ian since January 1st and my experience has been nothing but positive! I have a number of autoimmune issues I have been battling since my teens and I am now 30 and wanted to get my health right as a new parent. Dr Ian exceeded my expectations and I plan to continue working with him on this health journey. We have made improvements to my well being that pharmaceuticals could never do, as they do not address the root causes. Stevie the functional nutritionist is also incredibly knowledgeable and very helpful in making the transition to a healthier lifestyle and diet as smooth as possible. If you want a compassionate Dr who will stop at nothing to get to the bottom of stubborn health problems, I highly recommend Dr Autoimmune and his team.

I highly recommend Dr. Ian and everyone on his team. I'm a registered nurse and struggled for years getting doctors to listen. I really feel like he listened to me and found the causes of my problems. I'm down 90 lbs since April and feel better than I have in years.

I'm so greatful he is working with me to correct some of my lab values and he even found several gene mutations that were greatly impacting my life. Every other doctor would take 1 look at me and tell me to eat less and move more; before ever asking what I ate. Not Dr. Ian. He did labs first then we talked and came up with a plan. Stevie his nutritionists has been great and I've learned so much.

Today I was able to buy the same size jeans I wore in hs and they fit!! It's amazing...they are amazing. Do the program. You are worth it!

I have been working with Dr. Ian since late June of this year in 2024, and I can 100% honestly say his work has changed my life. Before going to Dr. Ian, I had been to soooo many doctors, including other functional medicine providers, with no help or end in sight with the autoimmune thyroid issues I had been experiencing. No one could figure out what was going on and my family and I were wasting thousands of dollars on these other functional medicine doctors with zero results. It felt hopeless.

Because of working with Dr. Ian, I am finally getting better and I am so very grateful to be working with him and Stevie, the nutritionist. Both Dr. Ian and Stevie are so understanding about the toll having an autoimmune disease can take when nothing is working. I would recommend working with them to anyone struggling with an autoimmune disease or complex health issues in general to see them, it is worth the money when these results have absolutely changed my health and life for the better! So grateful for Dr. Ian and everyone else who has kindly helped me at his office:)!!!
I am pain free after having 5 years of inflammation and joint pain.
I have lost about 25 pounds, my joints don't hurt anymore and I have more energy.
Within a month I lost 20 pounds. I no longer have brain fog or bloating. My energy is back.
I feel like a new person. I have energy again. My pain is gone and I finally feel like myself.
After years of feeling dismissed by other doctors, Dr. Hollaman actually listened. His team dug into the root cause and finally I have answers, and a plan that's working.
The remote care has been life-changing. I get expert functional-medicine support from home and my symptoms are 80% better.
My anxiety and depression have improved more in six months here than in ten years of conventional treatment. This team gets it.
I was skeptical at first, but the personalized plan and regular check-ins made all the difference. My labs finally look normal.
Dr. Autoimmune is the first practice that treated me like a whole person, not a diagnosis. My gut is healing and my energy is back.
The comprehensive lab work uncovered issues no one else even thought to check for. I finally understand what's driving my flares.

results.bodyText: +1 (303) 882-8447npc@drautoimmune.comHomeAbout UsServicesConditionsPatient StoriesBlogShopContact UsBook your Discovery CallA Different Kind of Functional MedicineAbout UsBorn from lived experience. Built for people searching for answers.Our StoryMost of the people who find their way to Dr. Autoimmune have already been through a long and difficult journey. They have seen multiple providers, received conflicting information, and still do not feel well. Our practice was created for them, for the people who know something deeper is going on and want a team who will finally take the time to understand it.We believe that every patient deserves clarity, connection, and care that looks beyond symptoms. That belief shapes everything we do.Our care is delivered entirely through telehealth, making it possible for patients across the United States to receive thoughtful, comprehensive support from wherever they live.0+Years of Clinical Experience0%Remote, Telehealth-Based Care0Pillars of Our Care ApproachFMCP CertifiedMeet Your DoctorMeet Dr. Ian Hollaman, DC, MSc, FMCPDr. Ian Hollaman became passionate about functional medicine after facing his own health challenges during graduate school. After months of worsening symptoms and little clarity from multiple providers, he finally found a functional medicine doctor who looked deeper, connected the dots, and helped him understand what was truly going on. That experience reshaped both his health and his career path.For more than 16 years, Dr. Ian has helped patients with autoimmune, gastrointestinal, thyroid, and chronic conditions that have not improved with standard care. His approach combines advanced functional medicine, nutrition, supplementation, and lifestyle strategies to create personalized plans that match each patient's unique needs.Dr. Ian provides all care through virtual visits, allowing patients nationwide to access thorough, personalized support without leaving home.Dr. Ian is a chiropractic physician, holds a Master of Science in Human Nutrition and Functional Medicine, and earned his functional medicine certification through the Institute for Functional Medicine. He has lectured nationally and contributed to supplement product formulation, but patients most appreciate his ability to listen, explain clearly, and uncover what others have overlooked.Outside of practice, Dr. Ian enjoys life with his wife and four children west of Boulder, Colorado, and spends his free time in falconry, hunting, gardening, and soccer.FNTP CertifiedMetabolic Coordinator / Functional NutritionistMeet Stevie ChaddockStevie Chaddock is a Functional Nutritional Therapy Practitioner and Clinical Nutritionist with a master's degree in Nutrition Science. She specializes in gut microbiome dysfunction and autoimmune conditions, bringing both clinical insight and genuine warmth to every patient interaction.Stevie believes that food is information, a reflection of physiology, habits, emotions, and lived experiences. With this perspective, she takes the time to understand not just what patients eat, but how and why they eat. Stevie uses this insight to create personalized nutrition strategies that feel supportive and realistic. Recent advances in research are helping us understand brains with ADHD, leading to the development of new treatment options that offer the promise of a brighter future for you or your child.ADD/ADHD spectrum disorders are often thought of as strictly brain-related. Treatments for these disorders are often focused on reducing symptoms. However, there is a strong link to what is happening in the brain to what is happening in the gut. Our functional medicine approach focuses on identifying the root causes behind brain-related issues.How Can Dr. Autoimmune Help?There is hope for happiness. It takes courage and commitment as well as powerful knowledge, support, and tools from an expert. Dr. Autoimmune and his team incorporate functional medicine, functional neurology, functional nutrition, brain mapping, neurofeedback and customized chiropractic care to help people with brain-based disorders.Our featured service for ADHD/ADD is neurofeedback. Inflammation in your gut sends signals to your brain, causing similar responses such as inflammation, stress, anxiety, depression and a host of other mental health issues.By restoring healthy gut function, we can make a huge impact on mental function. One of the first stages of autoimmunity can often be dysbiosis which isn’t always detected in regular bloodwork, which is why early detection is key to preventing disease progression. We look at over 85 different blood markers that traditional doctors don’t test for, ensuring that we have the best overall picture, so keep reading to learn more about dysbiosis and how it affects autoimmunity.What is Dysbiosis? Dysbiosisis a term that refers to the disturbance of the gut microbial flora where any of the following occurs, sometimes simultaneously: the loss of beneficial organisms, excessive growth of potentially harmful bacteria, and the loss of overall diversity in the microbiome. These intestinal bacteria are vital for healthy immune function and inflammatory response, as well as digestion, nutrient absorption, and so much more.How does dysbiosis affect autoimmunity? A gut imbalance like dysbiosis could eventually lead toleaky gut syndrome, chronic disease, and gastrointestinal autoimmune conditions such as IBS. Dysbiosis damages the gut lining and weakens the immune-gut barrier, resulting in a myriad of different symptoms from digestive issues like constipation, diarrhea, and bloating to chronic inflammation, brain fog, food intolerances, weight management issues, and more. Small intestinal fungal overgrowth (SIFO) and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) are also types of dysbiosis.Dysbiosis and depression: Recentresearchhas shown that altered bacterial populations can directly stimulate negative inflammatory chemicals which impact behavior. In fact, 2 antibiotics taken within a 12-month period of time increase your risk of a depression diagnosis by 40%, and to date, physicians are not taught how to mitigate the risks these medications have on our microbiome! However, if you can reduce the quality through medications, you can improve and sometimes radically improve the microbiome improving mood, energy, and inflammatory markers!Can you fix dysbiosis naturally? Yes, improvement is possible, especially with our team by your side! Long-term lifestyle changes are key to fixing dysbiosis and restoring your gut’s microbial balance, diet and nutrition are among the most important. Identifying triggers such as gluten, dairy, processed foods, and artificial sugars, along with treating any deficiencies like Vitamin D, are all part of a plan to reverse the effects of dysbiosis.How can Dr. Autoimmune help? Our functional medicine approach to autoimmunity and chronic disease means that we seek to find the “why” underneath your symptoms and find solutions that support the root cause. Clinical nutrition, lifestyle changes, environmental triggers, and stress are just a few of the aspects of your health that we consider. With years of experience helping people manage their autoimmune diseases, our experts are confident that we can help you find relief from your symptoms too. We also utilize cutting-edge supplementation to assist the body in repairing itself. TheLeaky Gut Trioincludes 3 of our most powerful supplements–Prebio-Power, a guar gum prebiotic supplement specially formulated to provide you 7 grams of highly absorbable sun fiber per serving;ImmunoPower, a blend of probiotics and nutrients designed to support overall immune health and the activation of T regulatory cells; andGut Power, a restorative gut support supplements with ingredients such as Betaine HCL and Zinc Carnosine. results.bodyText: +1 (303) 882-8447npc@drautoimmune.comHomeAbout UsServicesConditionsPatient StoriesBlogShopContact UsBook your Discovery CallBlogIf My ANA Is Positive Do I Have an Autoimmune Disease?July 20, 2026•9 minutesIf you have ever opened your lab results and seen the words positive ANA, you know how unsettling it can be. For many people, it feels like a quiet alarm bell. You may not feel well. You may have been dealing with fatigue, joint pain, rashes, digestive issues, brain fog, or mysterious symptoms that never quite add up. You know something feels off, but every appointment seems to end with more questions than answers. Then suddenly a blood test comes back abnormal, yet no one can tell you what it really means. Some people are told not to worry about it. Others are told to come back when things get worse. Some are sent from doctor to doctor, collecting opinions but not answers. You are left stuck in between knowing something is wrong but not having a clear diagnosis or a path forward. You leave the appointment relieved that nothing serious was found, but at the same time frustrated because you still do not feel well. You are stuck in a strange place between being told you are fine and knowing something is not right. That uncertainty can be exhausting, especially when symptoms continue affecting your energy, focus, digestion, joints, or overall quality of life. This is one of the most common situations I see in my practice. People come in with a positive ANA but no diagnosis, and they feel confused, scared, and often dismissed. They know their body is not working the way it should, yet the system is telling them to wait. I am Dr. Ian Hollaman DC, MSc, FMCP, and I want you to know that a positive ANA is not something to ignore. It is not a diagnosis, but it is a message from your immune system. When you understand what it is actually telling you, you can take steps to protect your health instead of waiting for things to get worse.What ANA Actually Is and What It Is Not ANA stands for antinuclear antibody. These are antibodies that target the nucleus of your own cells. In a healthy immune system, antibodies are used to identify and neutralize threats like bacteria and viruses. When ANA is present, it means the immune system has begun to recognize your own tissue as something that might not belong. That does not automatically mean you have a specific autoimmune disease. It does mean your immune system is no longer fully tolerant of your own body. Think of ANA as an early warning signal.It tells us that immune regulation is changing. Another way to think about it is this: a positive ANA does not mean you have a specific autoimmune disease.It means your immune system is waving a flag and asking for attention. Many autoimmune diseases begin years before a formal diagnosis is ever made. By the time someone receives a diagnosis, the immune system has often been struggling for years beneath the surface. A positive ANA can be one of the earliest clues that this process may already be underway. In some people, this change stays mild and never progresses. In others, it is the first step on a path toward conditions like lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, Hashimoto’s, or other autoimmune diseases. When doctors see ANA, they often wait for more damage to occur before acting. From a functional medicine perspective, that is exactly backward. This is the moment when intervention can be the most effective.Why So Many People Have a Positive ANA With No Clear Diagnosis One of the reasons ANA creates so much confusion is that it is not tied to a single disease. It reflects immune activation, not tissue damage. Conventional medicine is built around diagnosing disease once organs are clearly affected. Functional medicine focuses on what is happening before that damage occurs. This is why so many people with a positive ANA but no diagnosis feel stuck in limbo. They do not meet the criteria for a named condition, but their immune system is clearly not behaving normally. In these cases, we often see patterns like chronic infections, gut permeability, toxin exposure, hormonal imbalances, or prolonged stress. All of these can push the immune system toward autoimmunity long before a traditional diagnosis appears.How Early Autoimmune Disease Develops Autoimmune disease rarely appears overnight. It develops in stages. First, genetic susceptibility and environmental triggers create immune stress. Then immune tolerance begins to break down. This is often when ANA becomes positive. Over time, if those triggers continue, inflammation increases and specific tissues become targets. Eventually organ damage occurs and a formal diagnosis is made. This is why early autoimmune disease testing is so important. When you identify immune dysregulation early, you can intervene before irreversible damage is done.Why Autoimmune Blood Work Is So Often Misunderstood Most people assume blood work gives clear answers. In reality, standard autoimmune panels are designed to confirm disease, not prevent it. They are very good at identifying late-stage autoimmunity. They are not designed to explain early immune imbalance. This is why autoimmune blood work explained from a functional medicine perspective looks very different. We look at antibodies, inflammation markers, nutrient status, and immune regulation. We look at patterns, not just positive or negative results. When you understand those patterns, the picture becomes much clearer.What A Positive ANA Is Really Telling You A positive ANA means your immune system is activated and losing tolerance. It means something is pushing it to misidentify your own cells as threats. That something might be in your gut. It might be a chronic infection. It might be mold or toxins. It might be unresolved stress. Often it is a combination of several factors that have been building for years. The key point is this. A positive ANA is not a dead end. It is an opportunity to change course. If you’ve been told your ANA is positive but no one has helped you understand why, it may be time to look deeper. Schedule a complimentary Discovery Callto learn whether there may be underlying factors contributing to immune activation.How We Approach This at Dr Autoimmune At Dr Autoimmune we do not wait for disease to become severe. We look for the root causes that are driving immune imbalance. We use advanced testing to evaluate gut health, infections, toxins, hormone balance, nutrient deficiencies, and inflammatory markers. Then we create a plan that supports immune regulation, repairs barriers, and removes triggers. The goal is to help the immune system calm down and regain tolerance.What We Test When ANA Is Positive When someone comes to us with a positive ANA, we do not look at it in isolation. We look at the immune system as a whole. We run detailed inflammatory and immune panels that include markers such as C reactive protein, ferritin, vitamin D, homocysteine, and immune globulins. These tell us how inflamed the body is and how resilient the immune system truly is. We also evaluate thyroid antibodies even when thyroid hormone levels appear normal. Many people with ANA positivity are already in the early stages of autoimmune thyroid disease, even before TSH or Free T4 change. Identifying this early allows us to intervene before permanent thyroid damage occurs.Gut Testing and ANA Positivity The gut is one of the most important places to look when ANA is elevated. A damaged or leaky gut allows food proteins, bacteria, and toxins to enter the bloodstream. The immune system then stays on high alert because it believes the body is under constant attack. We use comprehensive stool testing and intestinal permeability testing to evaluate the microbiome, digestive enzymes, inflammatory markers, and barrier function. We look for bacterial imbalances, yeast, parasites, and markers such as calprotectin that show whether immune cells are already active inside the gut. When gut health improves, many patients experience improvements in symptoms and overall immune function. Supporting the gut is often an important part of a comprehensive strategy for promoting immune balance.Chronic Infections That Drive ANA Positivity Hidden infections are another major driver of immune activation. Viruses such as Epstein Barr, bacterial infections, and other stealth pathogens can keep the immune system constantly engaged. We use immune and pathogen testing to see whether the immune system is fighting something behind the scenes. When these infections are addressed properly, the immune system often becomes calmer because it no longer has to stay in a state of defense.Mold and Environmental Toxins Mold exposure and environmental toxins are powerful immune disruptors. They damage the gut lining, overwhelm detox pathways, and force the immune system to remain activated. We use urine and blood testing to identify mold metabolites and detoxification capacity. If these are present, we support detox pathways and help patients reduce ongoing exposure so the immune system can finally stand down.What Our Functional Medicine Protocol Looks Like When you come to Dr Autoimmune with a positive ANA, we build a personalized plan based on what is driving your immune activation. First, we remove triggers, whether they are infections, mold, food reactions, or toxic exposures. Second, we repair what has been damaged, especially the gut lining and detox systems. Third, we regulate the immune system by restoring nutrient levels, hormone balance, and nervous system function. This approach focuses on identifying and addressing factors that may be contributing to immune dysregulation. By reducing immune stressors and supporting overall health, many patients experience improvements in symptoms and immune markers over time.Why This Matters More Than You Think Autoimmune disease becomes harder to reverse once organ damage begins. When immune imbalance is identified early, the body has a much greater chance to heal. A positive ANA is not a diagnosis, nor is it a predictor of a future set in stone. It is a signal.What A Positive ANA May Be Trying To Tell You One of the hardest parts about a positive ANA is not the lab result itself. It is the uncertainty that comes with it. You know something does not feel right. You are tired more often than you should be. Your joints may ache. Your digestion may have changed. Your energy is not what it used to be. Yet every appointment seems to end with more questions than answers. Many people are told to wait and see what happens next. The problem is that waiting can feel incredibly frustrating when you are the one living with the symptoms every day. A positive ANA is not a diagnosis, but it is a clue. It may be one of the earliest signs that your immune system is under stress and that something deeper deserves attention. In many cases, autoimmune processes begin years before a diagnosis is ever made. By the time a condition finally has a name, the body has often been struggling for much longer than people realize. That does not mean you should panic. It does mean you should be curious. Instead of asking, “Do I have an autoimmune disease?” a better question may be, “Why is my immune system sending this signal in the first place?” At Dr. Autoimmune, we believe those questions deserve answers. If you have a positive ANA and still do not feel like yourself, you do not have to keep wondering whether what you are experiencing is normal or whether you should simply wait for things to get worse before taking action. If you are ready to better understand what your labs may be trying to tell you and whether there are deeper factors contributing to your symptoms, click here to book a complimentary Discovery Call. You can also learn more about Dr. Ian Hollaman DC, MSc, FMCP, and our approach to root cause autoimmune careby visiting our About page While you’re here, check out this great video Dr. Autoimmune did on TikTok about, If My ANA Is Positive, Do I Have an Autoimmune Disease?Ready to Find Your Root Cause?Book a discovery call and talk through your symptoms with our team, no obligation.Book your Discovery CallRecent BlogsRoot Causes of Anemia and Low FerritinSeptember 10, 2026Leaky Gut Signs, Causes, and Functional FixesAugust 26, 2026POTS Treatment: Looking Beyond Salt and Medications with Functional MedicineAugust 12, 2026Autoimmune Thyroid Symptoms When TSH Looks NormalJuly 31, 2026View All PostsAt Dr. Autoimmune, we provide personalized, root-cause care to uncover the source of your symptoms and support long-term wellness.+1 (303) 882-8447npc@drautoimmune.comBoulder, CO· Nationwide remote careBook your Discovery Call→Quick LinksHomeAbout UsFeatured InterviewsBlogLearnAreas We ServeLive Webinar ScheduleStoreContact UsShopServicesBook New Patient EvaluationConditions We SupportWellness ServicesPatient PortalPatient StoriesBook An AppointmentConditionsThyroid ConditionsHashimoto's ThyroiditisGraves DiseaseRheumatoid ArthritisType 1 DiabetesInflammatory Bowel DiseaseCeliac & Gluten IntoleranceMultiple Sclerosis© 2026 Dr. Autoimmune. results.bodyText: +1 (303) 882-8447npc@drautoimmune.comHomeAbout UsServicesConditionsPatient StoriesBlogShopContact UsBook your Discovery CallBlogI Eat Clean Why Do I Still Feel Sick?July 13, 2026•7 minutesIf you are here, there is a very good chance you are doing everything right on paper and yet you still feel awful. You cut out gluten, stopped eating sugar, avoided dairy, read ingredient labels, bought organic, took supplements, drank green smoothies, and even tried meal prep. On the outside it looks like you are doing everything you are supposed to do, yet on the inside your body still feels inflamed, tired, and unpredictable. You wake up exhausted even after a full night of sleep. Your joints feel stiff when you get out of bed. Your digestion never quite feels right. Your brain feels foggy and slow, and your mood can shift for no clear reason. At some point the frustration turns into something heavier, and you start to wonder if your body is broken or if this is just how life is going to feel now. Let me say this clearly. If you are asking yourself why do I feel sick even eating healthy, the problem is not that you are failing. The problem is that food is only one piece of a much larger immune and metabolic puzzle that most people are never shown how to look at. I am Dr. Ian Hollaman DC, MSc, FMCP, and I work with people every day who followed every rule they were given and still did not get better. Many of them come in discouraged and even embarrassed because they think they must be doing something wrong. In reality they were never taught what actually drives autoimmune disease and chronic inflammation in the first place. So let us talk about what is really happening when you have autoimmune symptoms despite a clean diet and why a root cause functional medicine approach is often the missing piece.Why Diet Alone Rarely Solves Autoimmune Illness Diet absolutely matters. What you eat can either calm inflammation or make it worse, and I will never downplay its importance. But diet is not the same thing as immune regulation. Autoimmune disease is not simply a food sensitivity problem. It is a nervous system and immune system that have lost the ability to properly regulate themselves. Many people are told that if they just remove gluten, dairy, sugar, or processed foods, everything will fall into place. For some people that does help, at least at first. For many others it does not. They clean up their diet and may feel slightly better for a short time, but then progress stalls and symptoms slowly creep back. That is usually the moment when frustration sets in and people start wondering what they are missing. The reason this happens is simple. Diet can remove some of the sparks that irritate the immune system, but it does not always put out the fire that is already burning underneath. If you have cleaned up your diet but still struggle with fatigue, brain fog, or autoimmune symptoms, it may be a sign that deeper drivers are present. You canschedule a discovery call with our team hereto learn what may be happening beneath the surface.The Real Drivers That Keep You Sick When someone tells me they are eating well but still feel terrible, there are almost always deeper drivers at work. One of the biggest is gut dysfunction. Your gut is where the majority of your immune system lives. If the gut lining is damaged or inflamed, immune cells are constantly being exposed to things they should never see. Food particles, bacteria, and toxins slip into the bloodstream and trigger immune reactions that never fully shut off. So you can eat clean food, but if your gut barrier is compromised, your immune system is still on high alert. Chronic infections are another common driver. These can be bacterial, viral, parasitic, or fungal, and many of them do not show up on routine testing. They quietly stress the immune system day after day, keeping inflammation high even when everything else looks healthy. Toxins such as mold, heavy metals, and environmental chemicals are another huge piece. These disrupt immune balance and overwhelm detox pathways. If your body cannot clear them efficiently, inflammation becomes chronic, no matter how clean your diet is. Stress also plays a major role. Ongoing emotional stress, poor sleep, trauma, or a nervous system stuck in fight or flight mode all change how your immune system behaves. They alter gut function, hormone levels, and immune signaling in ways that block healing. When these factors are present, food alone is simply not enough. If you’ve cleaned up your diet but still struggle with fatigue, brain fog, digestive issues, or autoimmune symptoms, it may be a sign that deeper drivers are present. Many people spend years trying to find the perfect diet when the real issue is that underlying factors such as gut dysfunction, chronic infections, toxin exposure, nervous system dysregulation, or immune imbalances have never been fully investigated. Identifying those hidden contributors is often the difference between temporary symptom management and meaningful progress. You can click here to book a complimentary Discovery Call and learn whether there may be deeper immune, metabolic, gut, toxin, or nervous system factors contributing to your symptoms.Why You Might Feel Worse When You Try to Eat Better This part surprises a lot of people. Some patients actually feel worse when they clean up their diet. They remove inflammatory foods, increase vegetables, and add supplements, and suddenly their symptoms flare. They feel bloated, tired, foggy, or inflamed. This happens because when you reduce obvious inflammatory inputs, the body often starts mobilizing stored toxins and pathogens. If your detox systems and gut are not ready to handle that, those toxins circulate through the body and make you feel worse. People assume they are reacting to healthy food when in reality their body is finally trying to clear out deeper problems.The Difference Between Eating Healthy and Healing Eating healthy is about supplying nutrients. Healing is about restoring balance. You can eat the right foods and still have a nervous system that is locked in survival mode. You can have perfect macros and still have a gut microbiome that is out of balance. You can eat beautifully and still have immune triggers hiding in your tissues. This is why so many people with autoimmune symptoms -despite a clean diet- feel stuck. They are doing what they were told, but they are not addressing the deeper reasons their immune system is misfiring.Why Root Cause Functional Medicine Changes Everything This is where root cause functional medicine becomes so powerful. Instead of asking what diet you should follow, we ask why your immune system is activated in the first place. We look at the gut, infections, toxins, nutrient status, hormone balance, stress physiology, and inflammatory markers. When you understand what is driving the immune response, you can build a plan that actually restores regulation instead of just suppressing symptoms. This is not about chasing the next supplement or the next elimination diet. It is about removing the obstacles that are preventing your body from healing.Why So Many People Blame Themselves One of the hardest things I see is how much people blame themselves. They think if they just had more discipline or followed the diet more strictly they would get better. They think they must be doing something wrong. The truth is your immune system may not be misfiring because you ate the wrong thing. It is responding to a complex combination of stressors that build up over time. Your body is not punishing you. It is asking for help.How We Approach This at Dr Autoimmune At Dr Autoimmune we do not guess. We test. We use advanced lab work to understand what is driving immune activation. We look at the gut microbiome, intestinal permeability, infections, toxin exposure, inflammation, and nutrient status. Then we create a plan that supports detox, repairs the gut, calms the immune system, and restores metabolic balance. Food becomes one part of a comprehensive strategy instead of the only tool you are given.When Eating Healthy Is Not Enough If you have spent months or years changing your diet and still do not feel like yourself, it may be time to stop asking what foods you should remove and start asking what deeper factors may be preventing your body from functioning the way it should. Many people with autoimmune symptoms, chronic inflammation, digestive issues, fatigue, brain fog, and unexplained health problems become trapped in an endless cycle of trying new diets, new supplements, and new restrictions. They assume they have not found the right plan yet when, in reality, they may be missing the bigger picture. At Dr. Autoimmune, we know that real healing is about more than just food. While nutrition is an important part of the equation, many people continue struggling because deeper immune, metabolic, digestive, infectious, toxic, or nervous system factors have never been fully addressed. The goal is not simply to manage symptoms better. The goal is to understand why those symptoms are happening in the first place. If this article feels like it is describing your experience, that may be a sign that it is time to look beyond diet alone and begin investigating what may be happening beneath the surface. If you are ready to explore whether there are hidden factors contributing to your symptoms, click here to book a complimentary Discovery Call. results.bodyText: +1 (303) 882-8447npc@drautoimmune.comHomeAbout UsServicesConditionsPatient StoriesBlogShopContact UsBook your Discovery CallBlogThe Hidden Link Between Gut Health and Autoimmune DiseaseJuly 28, 2026•12 minutesIf you have been living with autoimmune symptoms or unexplained health issues, chances are you have heard the word gut thrown around more times than you can count. Maybe a doctor mentioned it in passing. Maybe someone in a support group swore that cutting out gluten fixed everything. Maybe you tried probiotics, removed dairy, eliminated gluten, switched to an anti-inflammatory diet, or spent months trying to eat cleaner, hoping this would finally be the answer. Yet despite all of that, you still do not feel like yourself. You may wake up exhausted even after a full night’s sleep. Your joints ache for no obvious reason. Brain fog makes it hard to focus. Your skin keeps flaring, your anxiety feels worse, or your autoimmune symptoms seem to come and go without any clear explanation. After a while, it becomes frustrating because you are doing everything you have been told to do, but your body still is not responding the way you hoped. What makes this even more confusing is that gut problems do not always feel like gut problems. One of the biggest myths about gut health is that it always causes digestive symptoms. In reality, many people with significant gut dysfunction have little or no stomach pain at all. Instead, they struggle with fatigue, joint pain, brain fog, skin flare ups, anxiety, hormone imbalances, or autoimmune symptoms while their digestion seems relatively normal. I am Dr. Ian Hollaman, DC, MSc, FMCP, and one of the most common things I see in practice is people with autoimmune disease who were never properly evaluated for gut dysfunction. When we finally look there, everything starts to make sense in a way it never did before.Why The Gut Sits At The Center Of Autoimmune Disease Your gut is not just a food tube. It is one of the most powerful immune organs in your body. Around seventy percent of your immune system lives in the lining of your digestive tract. That means every meal, every microbe, and every exposure that passes through your gut shapes how your immune system behaves. When the gut is healthy, immune cells learn tolerance. They see food and friendly bacteria and understand that they are safe. When the gut is inflamed or damaged, that same immune system starts to see danger everywhere. It begins reacting to things that were never meant to trigger it. This is one of the main reasons autoimmunity develops. One of the biggest misconceptions about autoimmune disease is that it starts in the organ being attacked. In many cases, the immune system has been under stress long before symptoms ever appear. By the time someone develops an autoimmune diagnosis, the underlying imbalance may have been building for years.What Leaky Gut Really Means In Real Life One of the most important concepts in autoimmunity is intestinal permeability, often called leaky gut. This happens when the tight junctions that hold the gut lining together become loose. When that barrier breaks down, partially digested food particles, bacteria, and toxins leak into the bloodstream. Your immune system sees those particles and thinks you are under attack. It responds by producing antibodies and inflammatory chemicals. Over time this constant stimulation trains the immune system to stay in fight mode. This is where leaky gut autoimmune symptoms begin. You may notice that foods suddenly bother you. You may feel inflamed for no clear reason. You may develop rashes, headaches, joint pain, or brain fog. These are not random. They are immune reactions that started in the gut.Why You Can Have Gut Issues Without Stomach Pain One of the biggest misconceptions about gut problems is that you have to feel them in your stomach. Many people with severe gut dysfunction have little to no little to no digestive pain; they may even be having normal, daily bowel movements. Instead they experience fatigue, autoimmune flares, anxiety, depression, or hormone problems. Your first sign of gut dysfunction may not be stomach pain at all. It may be brain fog that never seems to lift, fatigue that sleep does not fix, aching joints, recurring skin issues, or anxiety that seems to come out of nowhere. Many people spend years treating these symptoms individually while the gut continues driving inflammation underneath. The gut talks to the immune system and to the brain. When it is inflamed, the whole body feels it. This is why you can have gut driven autoimmunity even if you think your digestion is mostly fine. For example, some people feel wired but tired all the time even though they are sleeping. Others notice their joints ache for no obvious reason. Some struggle with mood swings or anxiety that comes out of nowhere. Others deal with skin issues like rashes, acne, or eczema that never fully go away. In many of these cases, the gut is inflamed and allowing immune triggers to reach the bloodstream, even though the person does not have classic stomach symptoms. You can also see this when someone eats a particular food and does not get stomach pain but feels foggy, fatigued, or achy within the next few days That delayed reaction is often immune driven rather than digestive. It is the immune system responding to what passed through a compromised gut barrier. If this sounds familiar, you are not alone. Many people are surprised to learn their fatigue, brain fog, joint pain, or autoimmune symptoms may be connected to their gut even without obvious digestive issues.Book your Discovery Callto see whether hidden gut dysfunction may be contributing to your symptoms.How The Microbiome Shapes Immune Behavior Your gut is home to trillions of bacteria. These microbes help digest food, produce vitamins, regulate inflammation, and train immune cells. When the microbiome is balanced, it supports immune tolerance. When it becomes imbalanced, it pushes the immune system toward inflammation. These bacteria are constantly communicating with your immune system. Friendly microbes send calming signals that tell immune cells everything is safe. Harmful or overgrown microbes send danger signals that activate inflammation. This communication happens every day, which means the balance of your microbiome directly affects how reactive or calm your immune system is. Antibiotics, stress, infections, mold exposure, and poor diet can all disrupt this ecosystem. When harmful microbes take over, they produce toxins and inflammatory compounds that damage the gut lining and activate immune cells. At the same time, beneficial bacteria that normally help keep inflammation under control become depleted. Over time, this imbalance can keep the immune system in a constant state of alert. Instead of reacting only when it needs to, it begins responding to things that should not trigger inflammation. That ongoing immune stress is one reason gut health plays such an important role in autoimmune disease.Why Food Sensitivities Keep Getting Worse When the gut barrier breaks down, food proteins enter the bloodstream. The immune system sees them as invaders and creates antibodies against them. Over time you start reacting to foods you used to tolerate. This is why people with autoimmune disease often feel like their diet keeps shrinking. They remove gluten, then dairy, then eggs, then soy, and eventually even healthy foods seem to cause symptoms. The problem is not the food. The problem is the broken barrier. Many of my patients tell me they feel like their list of “safe foods” gets smaller every year. They remove one food, then another, and sometimes feel better for a while, only to discover new sensitivities appear months later. Continually eliminating foods may provide temporary relief, but if the gut barrier remains compromised, the underlying issue has not been addressed. That is why supporting the health of the gut lining is just as important as identifying food triggers. Some of the most common foods people become sensitive to include gluten, dairy, eggs, corn, soy, nuts, and even seemingly benign foods like tomatoes or spinach. These foods are not inherently bad, but when the gut barrier is compromised their proteins look foreign to the immune system. Once antibodies form, eating those foods can trigger inflammation, fatigue, joint pain, headaches, or brain fog. This is why people often feel better when they eliminate foods at first, but then get stuck when the list keeps growing. Food is not always the problem. Sometimes it is what your immune system is reacting to because the gut barrier has been compromised. Simply removing more foods does not solve the underlying issue if the gut continues allowing those immune triggers through.Why The Immune System Loses Tolerance When The Gut Is Inflamed When the gut lining becomes damaged, the immune system stops being able to tell the difference between what belongs in your body and what does not. This is called loss of immune tolerance. In a healthy gut, immune cells are exposed to food proteins and friendly bacteria every day and learn to coexist with them. When the gut barrier is compromised, those same proteins and microbes can enter the bloodstream and are flagged as threats. The immune system becomes hypervigilant. Over time, this constant stimulation trains immune cells to stay aggressive. They begin producing antibodies not just against food and bacteria, but against your own tissues as well. This is one of the most powerful mechanisms behind autoimmune disease. Many people spend years chasing symptoms from one part of the body to another without realizing they may all be connected. What looks like a thyroid problem, skin condition, joint pain, chronic fatigue, or brain fog may actually share the same underlying driver: a gut that is no longer communicating properly with the immune system. Check out this great TikTok video by Dr. Autoimmune about how Leaky GutWhat We See On Advanced Gut Testing When we run functional medicine gut testing, the patterns are often eye opening. We frequently find bacterial overgrowth in the small intestine, imbalanced microbiomes, yeast or fungal overgrowth, and markers of gut inflammation. We also evaluate digestive enzymes, bile flow, and short chain fatty acids, which help us understand how well the digestive system is breaking down food and supporting a healthy microbiome. Low enzyme output and poor bile flow can leave food only partially digested, which may contribute to additional immune stress. We also look at markers of intestinal permeability that help us understand whether the gut barrier may be allowing unwanted material into the bloodstream. When these patterns are present, they often help explain why someone continues struggling with inflammation and autoimmune symptoms despite eating well and doing everything they have been told to do.The Gut Brain Connection In Autoimmune Disease The gut is connected to the brain through the vagus nerve and the immune system. When the gut is inflamed, stress hormones rise and neurotransmitters change. This is why so many people with autoimmune disease struggle with anxiety, depression, and brain fog. These symptoms are not simply “in your head.” They are often biological signals that the immune system and nervous system are under stress. One of the biggest myths about gut health is that it only affects digestion. In reality, your first clue that something is wrong may be difficulty concentrating, constant fatigue, anxiety, low motivation, or feeling like your brain just is not working the way it used to. As we work to support gut health and reduce immune stress, many patients notice improvements in their mood, energy, and mental clarity because the communication between the gut, brain, and immune system begins to function more efficiently.What Happens If Gut Issues Are Ignored When gut dysfunction is ignored, immune activation can continue beneath the surface. Over time, this may contribute to the progression of autoimmune disease. More tissues may become targets. Additional antibodies may develop. Symptoms that once seemed isolated can begin affecting multiple body systems. What may have started as occasional digestive discomfort or food sensitivities can eventually be accompanied by thyroid dysfunction, joint pain, neurological symptoms, chronic fatigue, skin conditions, or other autoimmune challenges. This is why identifying underlying contributors early is so important. The sooner you understand what may be driving immune dysfunction, the sooner you can begin supporting your body instead of simply reacting to new symptoms as they appear.How We Support Gut Health At Dr Autoimmune At Dr Autoimmune, we do not use one size fits all protocols. We build personalized plans based on what your testing shows. If there is bacterial overgrowth, we address it. If there is yeast or fungal imbalance, we address those findings. If testing suggests the gut barrier needs support, we focus on supporting the health of the gut lining. If digestive enzymes or bile flow appear low, we support healthy digestion. If inflammation is elevated, we work to identify and address factors that may be contributing to immune dysregulation while supporting healthy immune function. Every plan is individualized because every patient is different. Our goal is not simply to manage symptoms. It is to better understand the factors contributing to immune dysfunction so we can build a strategy that supports gut health, digestive health, healthy immune function, and the body’s natural ability to restore balance over time.Looking Beyond Individual Symptoms If you have been chasing symptoms from one part of your body to another, it may be time to stop asking, “What’s wrong with this symptom?” and start asking, “What could be connecting them all?” For many people, the gut is one of the missing pieces. It may be contributing to fatigue, brain fog, joint pain, food sensitivities, skin issues, anxiety, or autoimmune symptoms even when digestion seems completely normal. Understanding those connections can change the way you look at your health and help explain why so many treatments only address pieces of the puzzle instead of the whole picture. If you are ready to explore whether hidden gut dysfunction may be contributing to your symptoms, click here to book a Discovery Call.Every step of this process takes place through secure telehealth visits, giving you access to a comprehensive team from the comfort of home. Dr. Ian Hollaman, DC, MSc, FMCP, and his team will take the time to understand your story, review your symptoms, and help determine whether a deeper functional medicine evaluation may be the next step toward understanding what has been driving your health challenges. results.bodyText: +1 (303) 882-8447npc@drautoimmune.comHomeAbout UsServicesConditionsPatient StoriesBlogShopContact UsBook your Discovery CallBlogThyroid Clues Behind Autoimmune Fatigue and ExhaustionJune 7, 2026•6 minutesFeeling exhausted all the time with autoimmune disease, yet being told your labs are “normal,” is frustrating and confusing. When you struggle to get out of bed, need naps just to function, or dread social plans because you know you will crash, something deeper is going on with your energy systems. One of the most common missing pieces is thyroid health. Chronic fatigue is not just a random symptom or a sign that you are not trying hard enough. It can be a clear signal that your thyroid and immune system are under strain. When we look more closely, we often find patterns that standard testing does not catch, and that is where a functional and integrative approach can open up new options.Why Debilitating Fatigue May Signal Thyroid Trouble Many people with autoimmune disease are told that fatigue is just part of their diagnosis. They hear things like, “your labs look fine” or “you just need to pace yourself.” Yet they still: Need caffeine to get going in the morning Crash hard in the afternoon Feel wired but tired at night Wake up unrefreshed, even after a full night in bed This kind of deep, ongoing fatigue often points to thyroid issues, even when standard blood work is in range. The thyroid helps set the pace for every cell in the body. When thyroid hormones are even slightly out of balance, your whole system can feel like it is moving through mud. By looking at the connection between autoimmune activity, chronic fatigue, and thyroid health, we can uncover patterns that are easy to miss. A root-cause, functional view does not stop at “normal” results. Instead, it asks why you feel the way you do and what is driving that low energy in the first place.How Autoimmune Disease Disrupts Your Energy Systems Autoimmune disease is not only about one organ or joint. It creates inflammation throughout the body. That inflammation can interfere with how your cells make and use energy. Here’s how that can play out: Mitochondria, the tiny “power plants” in your cells, struggle to make enough energy Hormones that control stress, sleep, and metabolism become harder to balance The nervous system stays on high alert, so rest is never fully restful The immune system can also directly affect the thyroid and adrenals. This creates a “perfect storm” of: Exhaustion that does not match your activity Brain fog and slow thinking Poor stress tolerance and mood swings As summer activities pick up, this often feels worse. More social events, travel, heat, and long days can show just how fragile your energy really is. You may notice that extra walking, time in the sun, or late nights with friends leave you wiped out for days.Thyroid Imbalances Hiding Behind Normal Test Results Many people with autoimmune-related fatigue have had their thyroid checked. The usual test is TSH, sometimes with free T4. If those numbers sit in the lab range, it is common to be told that the thyroid is fine. A functional approach looks deeper. A more complete thyroid view often includes: Free T3, the active thyroid hormone that powers your cells Reverse T3, which can block T3 from working well Thyroid antibodies, such as TPO and Tg, which show if the immune system is targeting the thyroid Patterns in these markers can reveal: Subclinical hypothyroidism, where you have symptoms before clear lab changes Poor conversion of T4 into T3, leaving you low in the most active hormone Autoimmune thyroid disease, even years before stronger lab shifts On top of that, low thyroid function is often linked with other imbalances. These can make fatigue worse, such as: Nutrient gaps, including iron, selenium, zinc, balanced iodine, and vitamin D Chronic infections that keep the immune system “on” all the time Gut issues, which can affect how you absorb nutrients and clear byproducts When we see ongoing fatigue with “normal” TSH, we look at this wider picture instead of stopping at one number.What Chronic Fatigue Reveals About Whole-Body Imbalances Fatigue is not a character flaw. It is a message. Your body is asking for help and telling you that the current load is too heavy. Chronic tiredness in autoimmune disease often points to deeper, system-wide patterns, not just a slow thyroid. These can include: Gut health problems, such as imbalance in gut bacteria or irritation in the gut lining Blood sugar ups and downs, leading to mood shifts and crashes Difficulty clearing everyday toxins from food, water, and the environment Nervous system strain, where you feel stuck in “fight, flight or freeze” At our clinic, we think of this as building a “fatigue map” for each person. We look at: When you feel best and worst in the day How weather, heat, pollen, or air quality affect you What happens with travel, social events, or changes in routine These clues help point toward which systems need the most support, from thyroid and gut to sleep and stress patterns.Functional Testing and Natural Therapies to Restore Energy When fatigue is long-lasting or life-changing, guessing is not enough. Functional testing helps show what is happening under the surface so support can be more targeted. Common tests in a root-cause fatigue workup may include: Comprehensive thyroid panel with antibodies and active hormone levels Adrenal rhythm testing to see stress hormone patterns over the day Gut microbiome and intestinal permeability assessments Nutrient status and key inflammatory markers The goal is not just more data. It is to guide practical steps that match your body’s needs. These may involve: Targeted nutrition plans that support thyroid, gut, and blood sugar balance Anti-inflammatory and thyroid-supportive foods Evidence-informed supplements when appropriate, such as specific vitamins, minerals, or herbs Sleep and circadian rhythm support to help you fall asleep more easily and wake with more energy Gentle, paced movement and stress modulation strategies As thyroid function steadies and triggers for inflammation are reduced, many people notice more stable energy, fewer crashes, clearer thinking, and better tolerance for seasonal changes and activity.When to Seek Help From a Chronic Fatigue Specialist It is time to consider specialist input when: Fatigue lasts longer than three months Tiredness is strong enough to affect work, family life, or social time Rest does not lead to real recovery Fatigue comes with autoimmune symptoms, thyroid concerns, frequent infections, or mood changes People searching for a chronic fatigue specialist in Boulder are often drawn to functional and integrative care, because they want someone to look at the thyroid-immune-energy link in detail. Although we work fully remotely, the depth of investigation is similar to what someone might hope to find with a local chronic fatigue specialist in Boulder or any other area. At Dr. Autoimmune, we see fatigue as meaningful information, not something to push through or ignore. results.bodyText: +1 (303) 882-8447npc@drautoimmune.comHomeAbout UsServicesConditionsPatient StoriesBlogShopContact UsBook your Discovery CallBlogWhy Do I Still Have Symptoms When My TSH Is Normal?July 6, 2026•10 minutesIf you are reading this, chances are you have already heard the same frustrating sentence that I hear from patients every single day. Your labs are normal. And yet you are exhausted. Your hair is thinning. Your weight will not budge. Your brain feels foggy. Your mood is unpredictable. Your joints hurt. Your motivation is gone. And deep down you know something is not right. You start wondering if it is all in your head, or if you are just getting older; or maybe this is just how life feels now. Let me be very clear right from the start. If you have normal TSH but still have thyroid symptoms, that does not mean your thyroid is working. It means your thyroid is being misunderstood. I am Dr. Ian Hollaman, DC, MSc, FMCP, and I have spent my career working with people who were told nothing was wrong while their bodies were clearly breaking down. That disconnect between what you feel and what your doctor tells you is one of the most damaging experiences a patient can have. It erodes trust. It makes you feel crazy. It keeps people sick for years. So let us talk about what is really happening when your labs say normal but your life feels anything but. Many of the people who come to us tell me they feel like they are living in someone else’s body. They used to wake up with energy. They used to enjoy exercise. They used to be sharp at work. Now just getting through the day feels like a marathon. They cancel plans because they are too tired. They dread social events because their brain feels slow and disconnected. Yet every doctor visit ends the same way with a shrug and a printout that says normal. That emotional whiplash between what you feel and what you are told can be just as exhausting as the physical symptoms themselves. You start to doubt your instincts, and you stop trusting your body. That is not a small thing.What TSH Actually Measures and Why It Misleads So Many People TSH stands for thyroid stimulating hormone. It’s a signaling hormone from the pituitary gland in the brain to the thyroid gland in the neck. It tells the thyroid how much thyroid hormone to make. Think of it like this. TSH is the text message, and the thyroid hormone is the actual package being delivered. Most doctors are taught that if TSH levels are within normal limits then the thyroid must be making and converting hormones just fine, but this is often not the case. Your brain can send a perfectly normal TSH signal while your cells are starving for thyroid hormone. TSH does not tell us how much thyroid hormone is being produced. It does not tell us how much is being converted. It does not tell us how much is getting into your cells. It does not tell us if your immune system is attacking your thyroid. Yet it is often the only number being used to decide whether you are healthy or not. This is why so many people with Hashimoto’s symptoms with normal labs get dismissed. Their immune system is actively destroying their thyroid tissue but TSH stays in range until the damage becomes severe. By the time TSH finally goes out of range, the fire has been burning for years. This is similar to checking the smoke alarm instead of looking for the fire. The alarm might not be going off yet but the house is already filling with smoke. By the time the alarm finally blares, the damage is already significant. Most people do not realize that the brain can adapt to stress and dysfunction by adjusting TSH output. It tries to maintain balance even when the system is breaking down. That adaptation masks disease until it becomes impossible to hide.Why You Can Feel Hypothyroid Even When Your TSH Is Normal Your thyroid does not work in isolation. It is part of a chain. The brain sends TSH. The thyroid makes T4. The liver and gut convert T4 into T3. The cells use T3 to create energy. At any point in that chain things can go wrong. You can have plenty of T4 but not enough T3. You can make T3 but not be able to use it inside the cell. You can have inflammation blocking receptor function. You can have stress hormones interfering with conversion. This is why functional medicine thyroid testing looks at far more than TSH. At Dr. Autoimmune: We look at Free T4. We look at Free T3. We look at Reverse T3. We look at thyroid antibodies. We look at iron. We look at selenium. We look at gut health. We look at liver function. We look at cortisol. Because your thyroid does not exist in a vacuum. Many people tell me they feel like they are walking through mud. Their legs feel heavy. Their mind feels slow. They sleep eight hours but wake up exhausted. That is what cellular hypothyroidism feels like. Your blood tests can look fine but your cells are starving for fuel. This is why you might still struggle to lose weight even though you barely eat. This is why you feel cold when others feel fine. This is why your hair falls out and your skin becomes dry. Your body is conserving energy because it does not have enough usable thyroid hormone at the tissue level.The Role of Hashimoto’s and Why It Is So Often Missed Hashimoto’s is an autoimmune condition. That means your immune system is attacking your thyroid gland. Here is the part most people are never told: You can have Hashimoto’s for years before your TSH ever moves. During that time your immune system is damaging thyroid tissue. You slowly lose hormone producing capacity. Then you start to feel worse and worse. But the lab that most doctors use stays normal. So you are told you are fine. You might be prescribed antidepressants. You get put on sleep meds. You are told to eat less and exercise more. Meanwhile your immune system keeps quietly destroying the gland that regulates your metabolism, your brain, your hormones, and your energy. This is why so many people with Hashimoto’s symptoms with normal labs go undiagnosed for a decade or more. By the time they finally get a diagnosis, they often feel like a shadow of who they used to be. Relationships suffer. Careers stall. Self confidence drops. People start blaming themselves when in reality their immune system has been attacking them from the inside.Why Medication Alone Does Not Solve This Even if you are on thyroid medication, many people still feel terrible. Why? Because medication only replaces hormones, it does not address why your immune system is attacking your thyroid. It does not heal your gut. It does not lower inflammation. It does not reduce toxin exposure. It does not calm your nervous system. It is like pouring water into a bucket with a hole in it. You keep needing more and more just to stay afloat. At Dr Autoimmune we do not stop at symptom management, we go looking for the fire. People often feel discouraged when their medication dose keeps increasing but their symptoms do not improve. That is because the underlying immune attack and inflammatory environment are still present. Until those drivers are removed, the body cannot truly stabilize. Book Your Discovery Call With Us Here.The Hidden Drivers That Block Thyroid Healing There are a few big drivers I see again and again. Chronic inflammation Inflammation blocks thyroid hormone from entering the cell. You can have perfect blood levels and still be functionally hypothyroid at the tissue level. Gut dysfunction Your gut controls immune balance and hormone conversion. If it is inflamed or leaky, thyroid problems follow. Iron deficiency Your thyroid enzymes need iron. Low ferritin alone can mimic hypothyroid symptoms even with normal labs. Stress and cortisol High cortisol blocks conversion of T4 to T3 and increases Reverse T3, which is inactive. Toxins and mold These disrupt receptors and drive autoimmune activity. Until these are addressed, no amount of medication will fully fix the problem. These are also the reason people feel stuck even when they follow every rule. They eat gluten free. They take supplements. They try to exercise. Yet they still feel awful because the real drivers were never identified.Why Functional Medicine Thyroid Testing Changes Everything This is where functional medicine thyroid testing becomes life changing. Instead of asking one question, which is: Is your TSH normal? We ask the real question, which is: Why do you feel like this? At Dr. Autoimmune we look at immune markers, at conversion, at inflammation and at nutrient status. We also look at gut integrity, toxic burden, and more! When we do that, the mystery disappears. The pattern becomes obvious. And when you understand the pattern, you can finally change it. People are often shocked when they see their full thyroid panel for the first time. They realize nothing about their body was random. It all made sense. That clarity alone can be incredibly healing.Why You Were Told Nothing Is Wrong I want to be honest here: conventional doctors are not bad people. They are simply trained in a system that only reacts when disease is advanced. Autoimmune thyroid disease develops slowly. Metabolic dysfunction develops slowly. Cellular hypothyroidism develops quietly. The system is not built to detect or reverse early dysfunction. It is built to wait until it is obvious. Unfortunately by then people have suffered for years.This is why patients often feel like they fell through the cracks…because they did! The system was not designed for people in the gray zone.Why You Are Not Broken If you have been struggling with fatigue, weight management, hair loss, mood, or brain fog and were told your labs are normal, you did not fail. The testing failed you. Your body is not weak. It is responding to stress, inflammation, immune activation, and metabolic disruption exactly as it should. Our job is to find the cause and remove it.How We Do This at Dr Autoimmune At Dr Autoimmune we combine advanced lab testing with root cause medicine. We do not guess. We measure! We identify immune triggers, we assess gut health, we evaluate hormone conversion, we look at nutrient deficiencies, and we check for toxins and infections. Then we build a personalized plan to restore immune balance and thyroid function. You deserve a plan that is as unique as your body.Why This Matters More Than You Think Untreated autoimmune thyroid dysfunction does not just cause fatigue. It increases risk for heart disease, infertility, cognitive decline, depression, and other autoimmune diseases. This is not something to ignore. Your symptoms are not small. They are a warning.Your Next Step If this feels uncomfortably familiar, that is a sign. You do not need to wait until things get worse, and you do not need to keep guessing. You can click here to book a discovery call and speak with our team about what is really happening inside your body. You can also learn more about Dr. Ian Hollaman, DC, MSc, FMCP, the amazing team at Dr. Autoimmune, and how we approach autoimmune care by visiting our About page here.Conclusion At Dr Autoimmune, we believe people deserve answers, not dismissal. If you have normal TSH but still feel like your body is failing you, that is not a coincidence. It is a sign that deeper imbalances are at work. We specialize in finding those imbalances and correcting them so your immune system, hormones, and metabolism can finally work together again. You do not have to live like this. If you are ready to understand what is really going on and start healing instead of guessing, click here to book a discovery call and let us help you take the next step. results.bodyText: +1 (303) 882-8447npc@drautoimmune.comHomeAbout UsServicesConditionsPatient StoriesBlogShopContact UsBook your Discovery CallBlogAutoimmune Skin Clues That Point to Gut Health TroubleJune 28, 2026•7 minutesYour Skin May Be Warning You About Your Gut Chronic rashes, mystery breakouts, or itchy patches that never fully clear are frustrating. Many people go through years of steroid creams, antibiotics, and new skincare routines, only to get short-term relief. It can feel like the skin is the whole problem, when in many cases, it is actually a surface clue of something deeper. Your skin is closely linked to your immune system and your gut. When the gut is irritated or out of balance, that stress often shows up where you can see it first: on your skin. This can look like redness, rashes, flaking, pigment shifts, or unusual sensitivity. In this article, we will walk through common autoimmune skin clues, how they can connect back to gut health, and why paying attention early can help you feel better overall. As more skin is on display during warm months, it is a good time to notice changes instead of only trying to cover them up.How Autoimmunity Shows Up on Your Skin First The skin often acts like an early warning system for autoimmune and chronic gut issues. Problems in the gut can quietly build over time. By the time digestion feels obviously off, the skin may have been sending signals for months or years. Some of the common immune patterns that can affect both gut and skin include: Leaky gut, where the gut lining becomes more permeable and lets more irritants pass through Immune over-activation, when the body is in a state of constant alarm Molecular mimicry, when the immune system confuses your own tissues with outside triggers Chronic low-grade inflammation, which can touch many organs, including the skin A simple one-time rash from a new lotion or plant exposure usually settles once the trigger is gone. We start to get more suspicious of autoimmune or gut-related patterns when: Rashes or hives keep coming back without a clear cause Symptoms move around to different areas Flares are triggered by heat, sun, stress, or certain foods Skin changes come with fatigue, joint pain, or brain fog Functional and integrative approaches look beyond the surface. Instead of only focusing on creams and ointments, we ask why the immune system is so reactive and how the gut might be involved.Common Autoimmune Skin Clues You Should Never Ignore Not every skin problem is autoimmune, but some patterns are strong clues that the gut and immune system need attention. Eczema and psoriasis are two big examples. They can show up as: Chronic itching or burning Dry, thick, or scaly plaques Flares that worsen with stress, certain foods, infections, or seasonal allergies These conditions are often linked with gut dysbiosis, which means an imbalance of gut microbes, and with increased intestinal permeability, sometimes called leaky gut. Hives, unexplained rashes, and redness can also point toward immune and gut issues. Chronic hives, rosacea-like flushing, or rashes that wax and wane without a clear allergy may relate to: Histamine overload Mast cell activation Microbiome disruption Vitiligo, alopecia, and other pigment or hair changes can reflect targeted autoimmune attacks on skin or hair follicles. These sometimes show up alongside thyroid problems, celiac disease, or other gut-related conditions. Nails and scalp matter too. Clues can include: Brittle, pitted, or ridged nails Flaky, inflamed, or very oily scalp Small sores or lesions that are slow to heal We often encourage people to keep a simple log of flare patterns, including: Foods and drinks Stress levels and sleep Seasons and weather Hormone shifts Skincare and hair products This kind of record can give a practitioner rich information about your immune and gut triggers.The Gut-Skin Axis and Why Your Microbiome Matters The gut-skin axis is two-way communication between your digestive tract and your skin. The gut microbiome, your community of bacteria and other microbes, talks with your immune system, hormones, and skin through substances they produce. When the gut lining is irritated or leaky, more particles from food, microbes, and the environment can enter the bloodstream. This can raise overall inflammation and make the skin more reactive. People might notice that they flush more easily, get rashes from mild triggers, or take longer to heal. Dysbiosis, or an imbalance in gut microbes, can: Increase toxins produced in the gut Change histamine levels Shift inflammatory signals that travel through the body Poor digestion and absorption can also deplete key nutrients your skin relies on, like zinc, vitamin A, omega-3 fats, and antioxidants. Without these building blocks, rashes, breakouts, and dryness can be slower to improve. A gut health specialist in Boulder, Colorado might use tests such as: Comprehensive stool analysis Food sensitivity or gluten-related testing Micronutrient panels Intestinal permeability assessments These tools help uncover what is happening underneath the skin symptoms.Summer Skin Flares and Hidden Triggers Warm weather often brings more sun, heat, sweat, swimming, and travel. For sensitive skin and immune systems, that is a lot of extra input at once. Some common summer triggers include: More sun exposure and higher temperatures Chlorine from pools or chemicals from hot tubs Sunscreen ingredients or fragranced body products Travel-related changes in food, water, and sleep Heat and UV exposure can increase histamine and oxidative stress in the body. If the gut and liver are already working hard, that extra load can make hives, redness, and rashes more likely. Summer foods and drinks can also stir things up. People often notice flares with: Alcohol, sugary cocktails, and beer Processed snacks or fast food while on the go Gluten or dairy at barbecues and gatherings High-histamine foods like leftovers, cured meats, or aged cheeses Some simple supportive steps include choosing simpler body products, staying well hydrated with water and minerals, getting plenty of fiber-rich seasonal fruits and vegetables, and easing into sun exposure instead of sudden long stretches. For those managing chronic conditions, remote support can work well in busy summer seasons or when travel and outdoor plans make in-person visits harder.How Functional Medicine Calms Skin by Calming the Gut A functional medicine approach starts by listening. We look at your full health story, including when skin symptoms started, how they have changed, and how they line up with gut, hormone, and immune shifts. Advanced testing may include: Comprehensive stool testing to look at microbes, digestion, and inflammation Breath tests for issues like small intestinal overgrowth Food sensitivity and gluten-related testing Autoantibody panels to screen for immune activity Micronutrient assessments From there, care plans are personalized. They may bring together: Anti-inflammatory nutrition tailored to your needs Gut-healing protocols to support the lining and microbiome Gentle detoxification support Stress and nervous system support Targeted supplements to help balance immune function Topical therapies can still be part of the plan, especially for comfort, but long-lasting change usually comes when the gut and immune system are addressed together. Because Dr. Autoimmune works 100 percent remotely, people in Colorado and beyond can work with a gut health specialist in Boulder, Colorado without having to travel, which can be especially helpful for those dealing with fatigue, pain, or mobility limits.Take the Next Step Toward Calmer Skin and a Calmer Gut This is a good time to pause and reflect on your own symptoms. It can help to write down your current skin issues, when they started, and any digestive or whole-body signs you may have brushed aside, like bloating, constipation, loose stools, fatigue, brain fog, or joint aches. A simple self-check is this: if your skin problems are chronic, recurrent, resistant to standard creams, or travel together with gut or systemic symptoms, it might be time to consider a deeper, root-cause evaluation. You do not have to choose between living with constant flares and relying only on prescriptions. An integrative, functional approach can help bring your gut, immune system, and skin into better alignment so you can feel more comfortable and confident in your body over the long term.Take The Next Step Toward Better Gut Health If you are ready to address the root causes of your symptoms, our team at Dr. Autoimmune is here to help you create a clear, personalized plan. Work with a trusted gut health specialist in Boulder, Colorado who understands the connection between digestion, immunity, and whole-body wellness. Now, I’m thrilled to extend a personal invitation to you for my FREE Webinar on “Healing Hypothyroid.” Hyperthyroidism is a condition where the thyroid gland becomes overactive, producing an excess of thyroid hormones. This can lead to various symptoms like rapid heartbeat, weight loss, anxiety, and more. Autoimmunity plays a significant role in some cases of hyperthyroidism, particularly in a condition called Graves’ disease, which I have extensive expertise in. In Graves’ disease, the immune system mistakenly targets the thyroid gland, leading to increased hormone production. I’m a leader in the field of functional medicine, with a strong focus on thyroid health and autoimmunity. With years of experience and a passion for uncovering the root causes of health conditions, I’ve become a trusted source of knowledge and guidance. More and more people are turning to functional medicine as an alternative approach to traditional healthcare, and I’m at the forefront of this movement.
